title: Polyglot bridge: legacy clients -> streamed structured-event tool invocations
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: many customers and partners still use legacy SDK patterns (blocking tool calls, callback hooks, non-streaming responses). The platform now exposes a single canonical streaming structured-event protocol for tool/function calling that enables incremental outputs, tool progress events, and typed structured results.

Objective: provide a compatibility bridge and canonical examples for TypeScript, Python, and Go SDKs so that teams can: 1) adopt streaming structured events incrementally; 2) continue to support legacy client code paths during rollout; and 3) have clear migration recipes and interop tests.

Scope: implement a thin adapter layer for each language that translates legacy sync/callback invocations into the streaming structured-event model (and vice versa where feasible). Deliverables: language examples, unit + integration tests, migration guide, one reference app demonstrating a tool that emits progressive progress and final structured result, and a small e2e perf comparison.

Out-of-scope: changing server-side protocol or introducing new persistent state APIs. This ticket focuses on SDK-side adapters and examples only.
design_decisions: Expose adapter as a small compatibility module rather than modifying core SDK signatures to minimize breakage.
Adapters will prefer ergonomic streaming primitives in each language (AsyncIterator in TS, async generators in Python, channels in Go) and provide simple blocking wrappers for legacy call sites.
Structured events will follow the existing schema: { type: "progress|tool_call|tool_result", meta: {...}, payload: {...} } to keep parity with server expectations.

Backpressure: language adapters will surface a configurable buffer size and drop/pausing policy; default is unbounded for user simplicity but docs will recommend conservative sizes for server-critical flows.
Security: do not change auth flows. Adapter only transforms transport-level message shapes; KMS/HSM and audit logs remain unchanged.
progress_updates: 2026-03-06: Spike completed — prototyped TS adapter that converts legacy callback tool runner to an AsyncIterator emitting structured events. Observed minor latency overhead (~3-5ms per chunk) due to serialization.
2026-03-08: Python adapter design validated with an async generator that yields incremental chunks and optionally returns final structured payload. Wrote initial unit tests for schema conformance.

2026-03-11: Go implementation prototype uses a buffered channel for events and provides both blocking CallTool() and StreamTool() API shapes. Added a compatibility shim to accept old-style func(ctx, input) -> output signatures.
2026-03-12: API review with DevX and Product — agreed on ergonomics, acceptance criteria, and docs outline. Assigned docs author and DevEx reviewer.
code_examples:
Python example (async generator adapter):

# adapter.py
from typing import AsyncGenerator, Dict, Any
import asyncio

ToolEvent = Dict[str, Any]

def legacy_sync_tool(input_data: Dict) -> Dict:
    # placeholder for sync legacy tool
    return {'result': 'ok', 'details': input_data}

async def legacy_to_stream(run_sync_tool, input_data) -> AsyncGenerator[ToolEvent, None]:
    loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
    # Run the blocking legacy tool in threadpool so event loop can stream progress
    fut = loop.run_in_executor(None, run_sync_tool, input_data)
    # emit a simple progress event while running
    while not fut.done():
        yield {'type': 'progress', 'payload': {'msg': 'running'}}
        await asyncio.sleep(0.05)
    result = await fut
    yield {'type': 'tool_result', 'payload': result}

# Usage:
# async for ev in legacy_to_stream(legacy_sync_tool, {'x':1}):
#     print(ev)
acceptance_criteria: Adapters implemented for TS/Python/Go with example repo and README.
Unit tests verifying emitted structured-event schema for progress and final result for each language.
Integration test that runs the reference app end-to-end against staging inference endpoint and compares final result to legacy path (within tolerance).
Migration guide + docs page drafted and reviewed by DevX and Product.
Performance regression <= 10% P95 latency for typical 1-2 chunk tool runs compared to baseline (measured in small e2e test).
